newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks seen lifted by U.S. bond rally,red chips.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen lifted by U.S. bond rally,red chips.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks are expected to move ahead slightly on Tuesday, boosted by positive overseas fundamentals and continued interest in China-related red chip shares, brokers said.
"The direction of the (U.S. 30-year) bond yield is quite encouraging," said Angus Shillington in institutional sales at Asia Equity. "We may also see some activity in red chips."
The 30-year U.S. treasury bond gained 15/32 to 99-5/32 to yield 6.69 percent in New York trading overnight. This is the issue's lowest yield since closing at 6.66 percent on February 25.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index eased 33.24 points to 14,361.36 overnight and the Dow Industrials closed 9.95 points lower at 7,772.09.
Brokers also said institutions were relatively inactive.
"I expect another quiet day with sideways movement," said a trader with a large U.S. brokerage. "The market has seen some big move lately."

Activity has been led by the retail sector and centred on red chips, he added. The Hang Seng China-Affiliated Corporation Index, which was launched on Monday, closed 194.60 points or 7.28 percent higher at 2,867.32 on its first day.
